title: Vue 3 Compiler PatchFlags: TEXT, CLASS, PROPS VNode Optimization

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In traditional Virtual DOMs, the computer inspects an entire building brick by brick on every update to see if anything changed. Vue 3's compiler puts bright neon sticky notes on the exact bricks that are dynamic: 'ONLY check text here' or 'ONLY check class here'. When an update happens, the engine reads the sticky note and skips inspecting the other 99% of the element.
progressiveExplaining.junior:
PatchFlags are numeric bitwise hints generated by the Vue 3 template compiler. When an element has dynamic text (`

{{ title }}

`), the compiler emits `/* TEXT */ 1`. When an element has dynamic classes (`:class="cls"`), it emits `/* CLASS */ 2`. When the Virtual DOM diff runs, Vue uses fast bitwise operations (`patchFlag & PatchFlags.TEXT`) to diff *only* the specific dynamic attribute, completely skipping static props and children.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, PatchFlags transform Vue 3's runtime from a brute-force recursive tree diff into a compiler-informed, type-specialized patcher. By encoding dynamic intent directly into VNode metadata at compile time, the runtime bypasses object property iteration (`for...in` diffing). This achieves near-compiled performance while retaining the full dynamism of a Virtual DOM.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: PatchFlags are defined in `@vue/shared` as a bitwise enum: `TEXT = 1`, `CLASS = 2`, `PROPS = 8`, `FULL_PROPS = 16`, `HYDRATE_EVENTS = 32`, `STABLE_FRAGMENT = 64`, `BAIL = -1`. In `patchElement()`, instead of diffing `oldProps` vs `newProps`, Vue checks `if (patchFlag > 0)`. If `patchFlag & PatchFlags.TEXT`, it sets `el.nodeValue = n2.children`. If `patchFlag & PatchFlags.CLASS`, it sets `el.className = n2.props.class`. Static attributes are never touched.

rosettaStone.react: Standard recursive Fiber reconciliation (no compiler-generated bitwise patch flags).
rosettaStone.svelte: Compile-time direct DOM update blocks (zero VNode diffing).

interviewGotchas.question: What does a negative PatchFlag (`PatchFlags.BAIL = -1`) indicate to the Vue 3 runtime?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of compiler optimization boundaries and bailouts.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `PatchFlags.BAIL = -1` instructs the runtime to **bail out of optimized diffing** and fall back to full, unoptimized recursive tree diffing. This occurs when a template uses features that prevent static analysis (such as custom render functions, dynamic slots without static keys, or manual VNode injections).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Render functions written manually with `h()` default to full diffing unless you explicitly pass patch flag constants.

interviewGotchas.question: What is `PatchFlags.PROPS = 8` and what is the `dynamicProps` array?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks precision regarding dynamic attribute optimization.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: When an element has dynamic attributes other than `class` or `style` (e.g. `:id="id" :title="title"`), the compiler sets `PatchFlags.PROPS` (8) and attaches an array of string keys `dynamicProps: ['id', 'title']`. The runtime loops *only* through the keys listed in `dynamicProps`, ignoring all other static attributes.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If an element has `v-bind="object"` (dynamic object spread), Vue must use `FULL_PROPS = 16` because the keys themselves can change dynamically.
